options.text: Have you ever heard of the Dorgeshuun?

steps.player: Have you ever heard of the Dorgeshuun?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Dorgeshuun? That old goblin legend. Lost tribe.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: In time of much-war there many tribes. Big High War-God send Dorgesh tribe to fight beardy-short-people in mountains.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, he send them to fight tall people with biting blades, that what I hear.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It was beardy-short-people, that how legend go.

steps.player: Make up your minds!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: It was tall people! That what old storyteller say!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No, beardy-short-people. That how legend always go, stupid.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: You stupid!

options.text: Do you want me to decide for you again?

steps.player: Do you want me to decide for you again?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That most stupid idea yet. If it happen it either happen one way or the other. You can't just decide which.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Yeah even goblins know that.

steps.player: It doesn't really matter. What happened to them?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Well, they say, 'We not want to fight,' so god punish them.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That silly. No goblin ever say that.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: What happen then?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: They lose battle, that why god punish them.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Ha ha! If they lost battle they all be dead!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, they losing so they run away, and Big High War-God punish them for running away.

steps.player: Who were they fighting again?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It was beardy-short-people in mountains.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No no, it was tall people.

options.text: What kind of god would punish them for refusing to fight?

steps.player: What kind of god would punish them for refusing to fight?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Shh! Must not question Big High War-God!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No, because he much bigger than us.

options.text: Well either way they refused to fight

steps.player: Well either way they refused to fight.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Yeah I suppose so.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Anyway then Big High War-God punish them. He turn their insides to stone.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Ha ha ha! That silly!

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Not as silly as green armour! What happen then?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: He put them inside stone! Big hole open in ground and they all go into cave.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That not punishment! Caves nice and cool.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: But then he close cave so they not get out! You not want to stay in cave all the time.

steps.player: Why were there punished again?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It because they run away from fight.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: No, it because they refuse to fight night before battle.

steps.text: What? Make our own tunnels?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: We hadn't thought of that.

options.text: Well I found a brooch underground...

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: That not look like goblin brooch.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Goblins not wear jewellery.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Well if it Dorgeshuun tribe they not know who won big wars. You should greet them with goblin victory dance!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: No no, you greet them with goblin tribal bow.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Doing bow make you look like a wimp.

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: It how tribes greet each other in old days.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Only if they wimpy tribes! Goblin salute strong!

options.text: So why is the Dorgeshuun tribe underground?

steps.player: So why is the Dorgeshuun tribe underground?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: They punished by Big High War-God.

options.text: Wait, you say YOU won the big wars?

steps.player: Wait, you say YOU won the big wars?

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: Well we must have done! We goblins! Goblins always win!

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: Actually we not know who won.

steps.speaker: General Bentnoze
steps.text: It was goblins I say!

options.text: Well why not show me both greetings?

steps.player: Well why not show me both greetings?

steps.speaker: General Wartface
steps.text: That good idea. Watch.

steps.player: Thanks.

steps.text: Bye then.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: A knight going on a dragon quest, hmm? What dragon do you intend to slay?

options.text: Elvarg, the dragon of Crandor island!

steps.player: Elvarg, the dragon of Crandor island!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Elvarg? Are you sure?

steps.player: Yes.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Well, you're a braver [man/woman] than I!

steps.player: Why is everyone so scared of this dragon?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Back in my father's day, Crandor was an important city-state. Politically it was as important as Falador and Varrock and its ships traded with every port.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: But, one day, when I was little, all contact was lost. The trading ships and the diplomatic envoys just stopped coming.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I remember my father being very scared. He posted lookouts on the roof to warn if the dragon was approaching. All the city rulers worried that Elvarg would devastate the whole continent.

options.text: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.player: I'd better leave that dragon alone.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: That's a relief. I would hate to see such a promising adventurer cut down in [his/her] prime.

options.text: So, are you going to give me the shield or not?

steps.player: So, are you going to give me the shield or not?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: If you really think you're up to it then perhaps you are the one who can kill this dragon.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Very wise. There are some monsters that are best left alone.

steps.player: Oh, no dragon in particular. I just feel like killing a dragon.

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: Who...who are you? How did you get in here?

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: Help! A surface-dweller this deep in our mines? We will all be destroyed!
If the player performs the Goblin Bow emote:

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: A human knows ancient greeting?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Perhaps you are friend after all!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Greetings, friend. I am sorry I panicked when I saw you.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Our legends tell of the surface as a place of horror and violence, where the gods forced us to fight in terrible battles.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: When I saw a surface-dweller appear I was afraid it was a return to the old days!

steps.player: Did you break in to the castle cellar?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: It was an accident. We were following a seam of iron and suddenly we found ourselves in a room!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: We blocked up our tunnel behind us and ran back here. Then we did what cave goblins always do when there is a problem: we hid and hoped it would go away.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: We meant no harm! Please tell the ruler of the above- people that we want to make peace.

meeting-the-lost-tribe-greetings.text: If the player performs the Goblin Salute emote:

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Eeek! The war-dance!

options.text: May I mine the rocks here?

steps.player: May I mine the rocks here?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: No offence, but we will not let you mine here until there is peace between the humans and the Dorgeshuun.

options.text: Why do the Dorgeshuun live underground?

steps.player: Why do the Dorgeshuun live underground?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Our ancient legends say that goblins were created by an evil god in order to fight in a huge war. This god sent the Dorgeshuun tribe to fight a battle where all would die.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: But our ancestors escaped by hiding in a deep hole in the ground where our god could not find us. Eventually an earthquake sealed the hole and they were forever safe.

options.text: The war is over now, so you can return to the surface.

steps.player: The war is over now, so you can return to the surface.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Even if the gods are no longer at war, I find it hard to believe that a tribe of peaceful goblins would be safe above. I have heard of humans coming down into the caves to slaughter our people!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: But even if we could return, we would not want to. We are adapted to living underground, and we have built a home for ourselves that we do not want to leave.

options.text: What was the name of your god?

steps.player: What was the name of your god?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Our ancestors did not speak his name, thinking that to do so would attract his attention. His name has been unspoken for so long that it is now entirely forgotten.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: That is for the best. We have survived perfectly well without gods, and we do not want a return to the old ways.

steps.player: What happened to your arm?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: I lost it in a mining accident a few years ago.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: This area is very unstable. That's why we put markers on the wall showing the safest path.

options.text: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

steps.player: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Certainly. Please hurry, you must avert the war!
Mistag shows you the way through the tunnels.

meeting-the-lost-tribe-using-mistag-s-br.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-using-mistag-s-br.text: We have more important things to think about than a brooch right now. We must prevent a war!

meeting-the-lost-tribe-trying-to-mine-th.speaker: Mistag
meeting-the-lost-tribe-trying-to-mine-th.text: We won't permit surface-dwellers to mine here until there is peace between our peoples.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: Have you any quests for me?

steps.text: Before starting the Rune Mysteries quest.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Well, it's not really a quest but I recently discovered this strange talisman.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: It seems to be mystical and I have never seen anything like it before. Would you take it to the head wizard at

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: the Wizards' Tower for me? It's just south-west of here and should not take you very long at all. I would be awfully grateful.
After starting the Rune Mysteries quest and still having the talisman.
After starting the Rune Mysteries quest and having lost the talisman.
After giving the talisman to Sedridor.
After starting the Rune Mysteries quest and having the Research package.

options.text: I've made contact with the cave goblins...

steps.player: I've made contact with the cave goblins. They say they were following a seam and broke into the cellar by mistake.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: And I suppose you believe them, goblin-lover?

steps.player: Well, they seemed friendlier than most goblins, and nothing was taken from the cellar.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Actually, something was taken. Sigmund has informed me that some of the castle silverware is missing from the cellar.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Unless it is returned, I am afraid I will have no option but war.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: What was I doing again?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: We are preparing to go to war with the underground goblins over the missing silverware. If you think the cave goblins are innocent you should present evidence quickly!

options.text: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.player: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: The priceless Lumbridge Silverware! It comes out only on special occasions. It was kept in storage in the cellar, but now the goblins have stolen it.

steps.player: So why did no one notice earlier?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: That doesn't matter. You'll never find it, because the goblins took it. So you can't stop the war!

options.text: Some silverware has gone missing from the castle cellar...

steps.player: Some silverware has gone missing from the castle, and the Duke thinks you stole it!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Oh no! We would never do such a thing!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: I assure you we took nothing from the cellar. You must convince the Duke we are innocent!

options.text: Where is the silverware you stole from the castle cellar?

steps.player: Where's the silverware you stole from the castle cellar?

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: What? We didn't take anything!

steps.player: You expect me to believe that? Perhaps Sigmund was right: you're just thieving little goblins!

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: Why would we want to steal silver? As you see we have much silver already in our mines!

steps.player: Well, the Duke says he will attack you unless the silverware is returned.

steps.speaker: Mistag
steps.text: The last thing we want is war! If we had anything of yours, we would return it at once. But we don't!

options.text: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

property-recovery-opening-sigmund-s-ches.text: If the player has the key:

steps.text: In the chest you find a set of H.A.M. robes!

steps.player: Sigmund must be a member of the Humans Against Monsters cult!

property-recovery-opening-sigmund-s-ches.text: If the player doesn't have the key:

steps.text: You don't have the key to open this chest.

options.text: You're a H.A.M. member, aren't you?

steps.player: You're a H.A.M member, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: What?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Well, so what if I am? It's not a crime.

options.text: Did you know Sigmund is a member of HAM?

steps.player: Did you know Sigmund is a member of HAM?

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Hmm, I had suspected it. But however much I disapprove of the HAM movement it's not actually illegal. I'll keep an eye on him though.

options.text: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.player: Tell me about the silverware that was stolen.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: The priceless Lumbridge Silverware! It comes out only on special occasions. It was kept in storage in the cellar, but now the goblins have stolen it.

steps.player: So why did no one notice earlier?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: That doesn't matter. You'll never find it, because the goblins took it. So you can't stop the war!

steps.player: Actually I have found it! You put it in the H.A.M. cave!

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: I... I... You're lying! I don't know what you're talking about.

options.text: Have you any quests for me?

steps.player: Have you any quests for me?

options.text: I found the missing silverware in the HAM cave!

steps.player: I found the missing silverware in the HAM cave!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Sigmund! Is this your doing?

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: Of...of course not! The goblins must have, um, dropped the silverware as they ran away.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: Don't lie to me! I knew you were a HAM member but I didn't think you would stoop to this. You are dismissed from my service.

steps.speaker: Sigmund
steps.text: But don't you see it was for the best? For goblins to be living under our feet like this... ugh. It doesn't matter how civilized they are: all sub-human species must be wiped out!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: That's enough! Get out of my castle now!

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I see I was ill-advised. Unless there is an act of aggression by the cave goblins there is no need for war.
The Duke writes a document and signs it.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: This peace treaty specifies the border between Lumbridge and the Cave Goblin realm. Please take it to the cave goblins and tell them I would like to meet with their leader to sign it.

If the player doesn't have the peace treaty:

steps.player: I, er, lost the treaty.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: sigh* All right, here's another copy.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.player: I have a peace treaty from the Duke of Lumbridge.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.speaker: Mistag
resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.text: A peace treaty? Then you will not invade?

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.player: No. As long as you stick to the terms of this treaty there will be no conflict. The Duke of Lumbridge wants to meet your ruler to sign it.

resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.speaker: Mistag
resolving-tensions-delivering-the-treaty.text: I will summon Ur-tag, our headman, at once.
Fade to black and a cutscene starts

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: ~ The Signing of the Lumbridge-Dorgeshuun Treaty ~

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.player: Your grace, I present Ur-tag, headman of the Dorgeshuun.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: Welcome, Ur-tag. I am sorry that your race came under suspicion.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I assure you that the warmongering element has been dealt with.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I apologize for the damage to your cellar. I will send workers to repair the hole.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: No, let it stay. It can be a route of commerce between our lands.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: [player name], Lumbridge is in your debt. Please accept this ring as a token of my thanks.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Duke Horacio
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: It is enchanted to save you in your hour of need.
The Duke hands the player a Ring of Life.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: I too thank you. Accept the freedom of the Dorgeshuun mines.

resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.speaker: Ur-tag
resolving-tensions-cut-scene-a-meeting-o.text: These are strange times. I never dreamed that I would see the surface, still less that I would be on friendly terms with its people.
The camera pans out to reveal Sigmund eavesdropping beyond the doors.

jump-e81510f1c01baf6e.player: Can you show me the way out of the mines?

jump-e81510f1c01baf6e.speaker: Mistag
jump-e81510f1c01baf6e.text: Certainly. Please hurry, you must avert the war!
Mistag shows you the way through the tunnels.

iZx9o7.player: Can you give me any advice then?

iZx9o7.speaker: Sigmund
iZx9o7.text: I only advise the Duke. But if you want to make yourself useful, there are evil goblins to slay on the other side of the river.

RlDs-9.speaker: Duke Horacio
RlDs-9.text: Thank you very much, stranger. I am sure the head wizard will reward you for such an interesting find.
The Duke shows you a talisman.

dFi-kP.speaker: Duke Horacio
dFi-kP.text: As you wish, stranger, although I have this strange feeling that it is important. Unfortunately, I cannot leave my castle unattended.

AHm0E4.speaker: Duke Horacio
AHm0E4.text: The only task remotely approaching a quest is the delivery of that talisman I gave you to the head wizard of the Wizards' Tower,

AHm0E4.speaker: Duke Horacio
AHm0E4.text: south-west of here. I suggest you deliver it to him as soon as possible. I have the oddest feeling that it is important...

Xlvoxu.speaker: Duke Horacio
Xlvoxu.text: Did you speak to the head wizard for me yet, adventurer?

Xlvoxu.player: No, I lost that air talisman that you gave me.

Xlvoxu.speaker: Duke Horacio
Xlvoxu.text: Ah, that would explain it. One of my servants found this outside, and it seemed too much of a coincidence that more than one strange

Xlvoxu.speaker: Duke Horacio
Xlvoxu.text: object would appear on my land in such a short period of time. Please take this to the head wizard at the Wizards' Tower, south-west of here, and don't lose it this time.
The Duke hands you the talisman.

fGthc3.speaker: Duke Horacio
fGthc3.text: The only job I had was the delivery of that talisman, so I'm afraid not.

fGthc3.speaker: Duke Horacio
fGthc3.text: No, all is well for me.

p5txee.speaker: Duke Horacio
p5txee.text: I've heard that the blacksmiths are prosperous amongst the peasantry. Maybe you could try your hand at that?
